title: Shared definitions of the threat model catalogues (threats, recovery actions, mechanisms)

entityClass.description: Name of a class of the setup ontology (table x-classes in SetupOntology.schema.json, drawn in SetupOntology.md); the loader checks it.

category.description: human: acts of people. physical: fire, water, force, environment. supply_chain: tampering before the item reaches the owner. defect: failure, ageing, bugs. software: malicious or faulty software and hosts. randomness: weak or manipulated generation. operational: mistakes and omissions in running the setup. legal: law, courts, authorities. third_party: vendor or provider business risk.

source.description: One cause. environment and owner act without malice; the others are actors against the setup.

phase.description: Lifecycle activity in which a threat can strike.

impactOn.description: Which items are affected, relative to the target entity. self: the target (for a secret: the secret as information). contents: everything stored in or at a Location or TamperEvidentBag, recursively through sub-locations and bags. intrusion_contents: what an intruder finds: everything in view, and a concealed sub-location only when it is the target itself (then the visible parts above it as well). area_contents: contents of the Location and of every location linked to it by `near` (close enough to be hit by the same area-wide event). knowledge: items in the Person's memory (backups with medium memory at the Person's location). access: contents of all locations the Person can physically reach. items: the secrets and plan copies carried by a Backup. loaded_seeds: seeds loaded on a SigningDevice. same_model_devices / same_vendor_devices: all other devices of the plan with the same catalog model or vendor. wallets: wallets that depend on the target (via a seed, a device, the coordinator or the descriptor). protects: what the target secret protects (devices using it as PIN, items encrypted with it, wallets whose signers use it).

impactKind.description: destroyed: gone for good. unavailable: cannot be used for now or until some action is taken. disclosed: an attacker obtains a copy or the knowledge. tampered: content or state is changed, replaced or wrong. controlled: the attacker can make the item act as he wants. misused: the holder uses what they can reach or know in an unintended way (impaired judgement).

origin.description: Review aid: whether the entry comes from the original notes or was added during the completion pass. Can be dropped later.

condition.description: Test on one attribute. `path` is an attribute of the item under test as it appears in the plan JSON (e.g. `kind`, `medium`, `generation`), or `catalog.<column>` for the item's row in a lookup table (device catalog for SigningDevice, metal backup catalog for Backup via its `product`, LocationKinds for Location). List-valued attributes match if any element matches. An attribute or catalog value that is missing or blank never satisfies `in` or `matches`, and always satisfies `not_in` and `not_matches` (unknown counts as not satisfied).

predicate.description: A named test that is too structural for a condition (graph or count questions). Implemented by the analysis; the name is the contract.
